PASS on the fake backend (last gate run: G1-G5 pass, G6/G7/G8 warn with the expected codes below, G9 pass). WHAT IT IS: the card's main model (models[0], scene.xml) served as a MujocoDriver; the step action is data.ctrl bounded per actuator by the model's actuator_ctrlrange (19 actuators: eight per Panda arm, two rail servos and one slider servo), the reset restores the mj_resetData defaults, and the state is time/qpos/qvel plus ctrl, tick, timestep and seed. The model file is read from the read-only clone at 2c4c322ad14edf521deceba3048e3844e0bf61d5 and is not copied into the package. WHAT WAS NOT COVERED: the real MuJoCo engine. MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip), and scene.xml needs a patched MuJoCo 3.3.2 build with the Chen wire plugin (README.md:93) plus fetched Panda and clip/peg assets (README.md:121-122). The fake backend (fake.py) is a stand-in mujoco module object: it parses scene.xml (which is CP1252, not UTF-8) for the actuator count, ctrlrange and joint dimensions, but integrates a placeholder first-order motion of the actuated scalar joints, loads no mesh, and resolves no contact, equality, tendon or wire-plugin constraint; the cable's ball joints stay at zero. No trajectory was compared with the real engine, no rendering is exposed, no physical device exists for this scene, and no hardware run was made. EXPECTED WARNINGS: G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because backends['fake'] is the stand-in mujoco module object (a module, not an upstream class whose fake surface could be recorded or checked); G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived inputs ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed. There are no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null).
